sections.name: architecture
sections.value: Doctrine: .agents/skills/pij-team/TENETS.md. Rust, functional core / imperative shell. Pure logic (json in → json out + decision) goes in a new module in crates/harnesses (it already owns Claude launch knowledge: crates/harnesses/src/spawn.rs passes --settings crossSessionInbound accept at spawn) — `crates/harnesses/src/claude_settings.rs`: `pub fn plan_inbound_accept(existing: Option<&str>) -> EnsurePlan` (pure) and `pub fn ensure_claude_inbound_accept(homes: &[PathBuf], clock) -> Vec<EnsureReport>` (shell, does the fs). Home discovery: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, $HOME/.claude, $HOME/.claude-alt if exists — see crates/daemon/src/claude_bind.rs:100-125 for how the binder already resolves a home (reuse, do not duplicate). Call sites: crates/cli/src/main.rs run_daemon (~L824, before the listening log line) and crates/daemon/src/registration.rs register() (~L36) when descriptor.harness == Claude. Spine event via the existing publish path used for delivery.* events. Doctor verb: add `doctor claude-inbound` to the CLI (crates/cli/src/main.rs verb table) — read-only. Tests: cargo test -p pij-harnesses for the pure/shell fn with tempdir; daemon integration under crates/daemon tests with a temp HOME. NO changes to crates/transport.

value.rationale: One new module, two call sites, one CLI verb. PM codes it, proves the live no-settings Claude run, then dispatches a cross-model reviewer (Claude opus seat).

value.name: claude inbound ensure
value.paths: crates/harnesses/src/claude_settings.rs (new) + its tests, crates/harnesses/src/lib.rs (export), crates/cli/src/main.rs (run_daemon hook + doctor verb), crates/daemon/src/registration.rs (Claude registration hook), crates/daemon/tests/* (integration)
value.responsibility: Ensure every Claude home on this machine has crossSessionInbound=accept; report and record what changed; expose read-only doctor.
value.interface: pub struct EnsureReport { home: PathBuf, before: Option<String>, after: String, changed: bool, backup: Option<PathBuf>, error: Option<String> }; pub fn claude_homes(env) -> Vec<PathBuf>; pub fn ensure_claude_inbound_accept(homes: &[PathBuf]) -> Vec<EnsureReport>; spine event kind `config.claude-inbound-ensured` payload = the report minus error, only when changed.
value.test_strategy: cargo test -p pij-harnesses: the five AC1 cases with tempdir; cargo test -p pij-daemon: boot twice with temp HOME, one event. RED-first with pasted red output.
value.note: Backups: settings.json.bak-<unix-ms>. Never touch settings.local.json. Never delete.

value.mode: solo-pm in the plan worktree (~/pi-hacking/fs3-claude-inbound-accept-global, branch 126-claude-inbound-accept-global)
value.note: Default: each coder gets its own worktree, branching off the PM's plan branch; unit lands back onto the plan branch (PM merges — coders never merge). Shared-tree work is the retro-proven #1 hazard (staged sweeps, untrustworthy greens) — only choose it for trivially disjoint single-wave work, and then file-scoped `git add` only, never -A. REMEMBER: fences partition WRITE intent, not the build — a mid-refactor sibling can still break your compile, so waves must respect build dependencies, and a broken workspace build is a PM composition concern, not a coder's to fix cross-fence.

value.steps: Build; cargo test workspace; harness checks (npm ci first in a fresh worktree); then the LIVE AC3 run. For AC3 use an ISOLATED daemon (--bind 127.0.0.1:<free> --state-dir <tmp>) — do NOT restart the production daemon (ask the prime, it will be refused); a hand-started claude with PIJ_RS_ADDR/PIJ_RS_STATE_DIR exported registers on the isolated daemon. Restore the operator's settings.json exactly afterwards if you removed the key (the ensure fn should have put it back; verify).

value.when: after composition (or after solo-pm coding), before the PR into main
value.inputs: plan.dd.md + this impl-guide + full branch diff; priority = plan promises, composition seams, interface drift, correctness, contract-test gaps
value.model_override: cross-model: Claude opus seat (pij spawn --harness claude), never GPT

value.text: Rewriting settings.json could reorder/reformat the operator's file: preserve with serde_json::Map preserve_order feature or a minimal textual insert; test byte-preservation of untouched keys.
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set per-seat could point at a home the daemon cannot see; registration hook uses the caller's env when available, daemon boot uses its own.
Malformed settings.json must never be clobbered — refuse + report is the only allowed outcome.
